coverageMatrix.completeness: Pip-tazo monotherapy covers the highest-mortality gram-negative risk; vancomycin is added selectively rather than by default.
gaps: Fungal coverage is not included initially — added only if fever persists 4-7 days despite adequate antibacterial therapy and neutropenia continues.

stewardship.deescalation: If cultures are negative and the patient is afebrile for 48 hours with ANC recovery trending upward, antibiotics can be discontinued. If an organism is identified, narrow to the most targeted agent while maintaining antipseudomonal coverage until neutropenia resolves if Pseudomonas cannot be excluded.

framework: Vancomycin (or other gram-positive-active agents) should not be added empirically to all febrile neutropenia patients by default — add only for specific indications (instability, line infection, mucositis, known resistant colonization).

Reassess daily; if afebrile and clinically stable with a reasonably short expected neutropenia duration, low-risk patients (per MASCC score) may be candidates for oral step-down or even outpatient management.
Empiric antifungal therapy should be reserved for persistent fever beyond 4-7 days on appropriate antibacterial therapy, not started upfront.
